title: ICC Pre-Trial Chamber authorises an investigation into the situation in Georgia
body:
On 27 January 2016 Pre-Trial Chamber I of the International Criminal Court approved the Prosecutor's request to open an investigation into the situation in Georgia. The investigation covers alleged crimes committed in and around South Ossetia between 1 July and 10 October 2008.

The Prosecutor submitted the request on 13 October 2015, and on 4 December 2015 the Chamber had received representations from 6,335 victims. The authorisation covers alleged crimes against humanity and war crimes, including murder, forced displacement and persecution, attacks on civilians and the destruction of objects.

The decision was the first time the court opened an investigation outside Africa, according to commentators. It was taken under the Prosecutor's own-initiative power, which requires judicial authorisation. The period covered runs from the escalation in July 2008, through the war of 7-12 August, to 10 October 2008, the date by which Russian forces were due to complete their withdrawal from the buffer zones around South Ossetia and Abkhazia. Georgia is a state party to the Rome Statute, which gave the court jurisdiction over crimes on Georgian territory.
